extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.use_case: This AI application serves airline customers by handling FAQ question answering, request triage and routing through a system of five specialized agents (Cancellation, FAQ, Flight Status, Seat Booking, and Triage) built with the OpenAI Agents framework. No multimodal capabilities (voice, image, or video) are present.
summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider / runtime:** Azure via GitHub Actions
- **Regions / HA / resilience:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** The deployment relies on a single GitHub Actions runner (ubuntu-latest) with no specified environment or resilience configuration, increasing blast radius risk.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret stores:** GitHub Actions secrets
- **Credential handling:** Credential reference `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` is used as a GitHub Actions secret placeholder; actual secret value is not exposed in the provided data.
- **Assessment:** While secrets are referenced via GitHub’s secret store, the absence of OIDC means long-lived credentials are stored as secrets, increasing exposure risk.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption at rest:** Not evidenced
- **Key management:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** No encryption configuration is present in the infrastructure nodes, leaving data protection posture unknown.

### 4) IAM / least privilege
- **Principals / service accounts:** `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` used as the IAM principal and service account
- **Scope / permissions / trust:** IAM scope is subscription-level; trust principals include GitHub Actions but no other constraints are defined.
- **Assessment:** Subscription-wide scope with a single trust principal violates least privilege by granting excessive permissions and lacking granular resource restrictions.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runners / triggers:** Ubuntu-latest runner with push and workflow_dispatch triggers
- **OIDC / credential flow:** OIDC is not used; credentials are exchanged via GitHub Actions secrets
- **Assessment:** Without OIDC, long-lived subscription-level credentials pass through GitHub’s secret store, increasing the risk of credential leakage or misuse.

### 6) Container security
- **Images / root user:** Not evidenced
- **Health checks / resource limits:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** No container configuration nodes are present, so container security posture cannot be assessed.

### 7) Top 3 prioritized actions
1. Replace secret-based authentication with OIDC between GitHub Actions and Azure to eliminate long-lived credentials.
2. Restrict the Azure Managed Identity scope from subscription-wide to resource-group or resource-level to enforce least privilege.
3. Define explicit deployment environments in the workflow to isolate production and non-production runs.

relationship_graph_md:
## Component Relationship Graph

- **Entry & Auth:** FastAPI exposes endpoints (Login, Me, Logout, Chat). Bearer Auth protects all endpoints. Chat endpoint is the main AI entry point.
- **Guardrails:** Two guardrails (Jailbreak, Relevance) run before agents, both using `gpt-4.1-mini`. No guardrail covers tool outputs or internal agent calls.
- **Agent Orchestration:** The Triage Agent delegates to Flight Status, FAQ, Cancellation, and Seat Booking agents. All agents use `gpt-4.1-mini`.
- **Tool Exposure:** Every agent has access to 5 tools: Baggage, Cancel Flight, Display Seat Map, Faq Lookup, Flight Status. No per-agent tool restrictions—over-privileged by default.
- **Data Stores:** Sqlite datastore has no incoming edges—no agent or tool is shown reading/writing it. This may be incomplete or data is accessed via an unrepresented path.
- **Risk Patterns:** All agents share identical tool sets, increasing blast radius if one agent is compromised. No guardrail monitors tool calls or outputs. External tool actions (cancellations, seat changes) are unguarded.
